findings.text: state-loader.js ends without a trailing newline, where its base revision and the sibling docs/ui/prompts.js both end with one; a cosmetic regression introduced by the large rewrite and not repaired by the follow-up fixes.

test_two_change_streams_recompute_discovery_once passes at the pre-guard serve.py revision (the interleaving lets the second stream's pop land before the first stream's rebuild), so the case does not by itself measure the guard it is named for; the deterministic companion test_a_report_keeps_a_discovery_newer_than_the_report is the one that fires without the guard, and the manifest says so.

item_verdicts.call_sites: verified production call sites: docs/index.html:25 loads /_ui/state-loader.js; docs/ui/shell-ready.jsx:81 awaits window.STATE_READY; docs/ui/shell.jsx:148 calls window.revalidateProjectState; docs/ui/plan.jsx:356 and docs/ui/crew.jsx:45 read window.STATE.
item_verdicts.diff: read the full 5340e028e..96b4d03e0: state-loader.js settles STATE_DERIVED_READY on the fallback path and stops inserting a discovery-only row; reckon/serve.py takes the observation stamp before the settle wait and skips a cached discovery newer than the reporting watcher's own observation while dropping the index rows and reuse window on every report; the head test file adds four cases.
item_verdicts.done_when: tests/test_page_paints_from_the_index.py runs the real loader under node with a recording fetch; readiness resolves on [/_index] alone with the derived set still empty, requested_at_readiness == [/_index] is the positive control that the background fetch is deferred, the later discovery merges onto the same rows in order, and the plan's named negative control reproduces (2 failed, EXIT=1); I reran the gate at head (83 passed, EXIT=0) and three negative controls myself.
item_verdicts.goal: §4 requires docs/ui/state-loader.js to fetch /_index/<project> first, paint its rows and resolve the first paint on it, then fetch /_discover/<project> in the background and merge the derived fields into the index rows without re-sorting, fetching a plan's body only when opened; the loader does exactly this and both defects the first review found are repaired at head.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits f83e38014..96b4d03e0 over base 4bdf93dde, both suite fields carry completed true with failure_count 0 and failure_ids [], and its counts reconcile with base-arm-4bdf93dde.log (75 passed 2 skipped EXIT=0) and head-arm-07e4597e2.log (83 passed 2 skipped EXIT=0); it states honestly that the two-stream case passes at the pre-guard revision.
item_verdicts.write_paths: `git diff --numstat 4bdf93dde 96b4d03e0` names five files, all within the node's effective scope (five declared paths plus the two added by the resume scope extension); tests/test_metadata_index_survives_restart.py is byte-identical to base and the discovery-only test changes only its docstring.

justifications.durability: the tests are deterministic — tmp_path fixtures, a private basetemp, a temp docs tree and a temp config home, no date-derived literal and no state outside the repository under test — and readiness is bounded by READY_TIMEOUT_MS so a non-resolving path fails rather than hangs; the deductions are that the two-stream case is timing-dependent (it passes at the pre-guard revision) and its guard depends on monotonic observation stamps, subtle enough to need the deterministic companion that pins it.
justifications.evidence: the measure is genuine and guarded — a positive control proves the background fetch is deferred rather than skipped (requested_at_readiness vs requested_after), row identity and order are both asserted, the base and head gate logs reconcile with the manifest, and I independently reran the head gate (83 passed, EXIT=0), the base arm (75 passed, EXIT=0) and three negative controls (the plan's readiness-gated-on-discovery mutation: 2 failed EXIT=1; a reverted arrival fix: 1 failed EXIT=1; serve.py at the pre-guard revision: test_a_report_keeps_a_discovery_newer_than_the_report 1 failed EXIT=1); the deduction is that the two-stream case does not by itself discriminate the guard, which the manifest states and pairs with the deterministic companion.
justifications.fit: the moved and added symbols are named by mechanism — assemble, derivedBlocks, projectRows, mergeDerived, arrivalKeyOf, _invalidate_tree_views, _invalidate_discovery_tree — with comments that state why the index is the first paint and why a new row is held as an arrival; no plan, phase, ticket or version label appears in code, symbol or comment, and there is no author attribute. The deduction is a cosmetic regression carried through the fixes: docs/ui/state-loader.js ends without a trailing newline (its base revision and docs/ui/prompts.js both end with one).
justifications.goal_fidelity: §4's index-first paint, the deferred in-place derived merge without re-sorting, the index-less fallback and the Python-computed derived values are all implemented as written at head, and both defects the first review scored down (the one-path STATE_DERIVED_READY and the discovery-only row inserted rather than held) are repaired and now covered by asserting cases.
justifications.scope_discipline: five changed files, all within the node's effective write scope (five declared paths plus the two added by the resume scope extension), no plan or index state was edited, and tests/test_metadata_index_survives_restart.py is byte-identical to base.

VERDICT goal: §4 requires docs/ui/state-loader.js to fetch /_index/<project> first, paint its rows and resolve the page's first paint on it, then fetch /_discover/<project> in the background and merge the derived fields (effective status and the ready set) into the index rows already on screen without re-sorting, fetching a plan's body only when it is opened, with the derived values computed in Python. At head 96b4d03e0 the loader requests /_index first, returns the assembled state as soon as it answers (state-loader.js:381-409) and runs mergeDerived one task later; both defects the first review found are repaired — window.STATE_DERIVED_READY is settled on every path (state-loader.js:397 on the index path, state-loader.js:532 with the assembled state on the fallback) and a row the index did not carry is held as an arrival rather than inserted (state-loader.js:334-338).
VERDICT done_when: tests/test_page_paints_from_the_index.py runs the real loader under node with a recording fetch; with /_discover never answering, readiness resolves on [/_index] alone with all four index rows present and the derived ready set still empty (test_readiness_paints_from_the_index_while_discovery_is_outstanding), and requested_at_readiness == [/_index] with requested_after == [/_index, /_discover] as the positive control that the background fetch is deferred rather than skipped. The second case resolves /_discover later and asserts the derived fields land on the same row objects (same_rows) with the order unchanged (test_derived_fields_merge_into_the_rows_already_on_screen). The plan's named negative control is executed and logged (readiness gated on the discovery response: 2 failed, EXIT=1). I reran the five-file gate at 96b4d03e0 myself (83 passed, 2 skipped, EXIT=0) and reproduced three negative controls.
VERDICT write_paths: `git diff --numstat 4bdf93dde 96b4d03e0` lists five files — docs/evidence/fragments/the-page-paints-from-an-index/page-paints-from-the-index.html (127), docs/ui/state-loader.js (348/226), reckon/serve.py (31/25), tests/test_page_paints_from_the_index.py (733), tests/test_served_loader_reads_discovery_only.py (11/10) — every one inside the node's effective write scope (its five declared paths plus reckon/serve.py and reckon/metadata_index.py, added by the resume-1 scope extension). tests/test_metadata_index_survives_restart.py is byte-identical to the base revision (git rev-parse both sides: 7d6df4944b7b3d7acde46ad88d57c093e720cfdc) and tests/test_served_loader_reads_discovery_only.py changes only its module docstring.
VERDICT manifest: read; status complete, commits f83e38014, ad6971e0d, c71819cce, 83207a0e0, 39d09daab, 5340e028e, 07e4597e2, 96b4d03e0 over base 4bdf93dde, both suite fields carry completed true (failure_count 0, failure_ids []), and the negative-control log is named. The counts reconcile with base-arm-4bdf93dde.log (75 passed 2 skipped EXIT=0) and head-arm-07e4597e2.log (83 passed 2 skipped EXIT=0); the manifest is honest that the two-stream case passes at the pre-guard revision and that its deterministic companion is the case that fires.
